subject: Onboarding: throughput & cost tuning plan (batching/prefetch/quant/routing)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: throughput & cost tuning plan (batching/prefetch/quant/routing)

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our call, I wanted to kick off a short, actionable onboarding plan that focuses on the cost / performance levers we'll use during your initial production ramp. High level goals you mentioned: P95 latency <= 250ms for user-facing endpoints, and token cost <$0.0008 on average.

Proposed initial scope (30-day focus):
- Batching: conservative session grouping, with per-route max latency cap for user flows.
- Prefetch / KV cache: configure prefix caching for common prompts and warm KV cache for long-lived sessions.
- Quantization profile: recommend 4-bit or 8-bit profiles based on inference quality tests; start with mixed-precision for sensitive routes.
- Routing policy: latency-first for release-critical endpoints, cost-first for batch/analytics endpoints; fallback to smaller model variants on capacity spikes.

Can Marissa take point on quant profiles and evaluation prompt set? Karthik, could you sketch an initial routing policy we can trial? Sean, would you own batching thresholds and cache TTL recommendations? Claire — if you can share a small set of perf traces and top-10 prompts (anonymized), we’ll run initial sims and propose tuned configs.

Attaching our onboarding checklist and a short template for the prompt set. I’ll schedule a 45 minute kickoff once we have the prompt/trace bundle.

Next steps:
1) Claire: share prompts + perf traces (attachment) by Wed 6/17
2) Redwood: internal owners will produce config proposals within 3 business days after we receive assets
3) Align on rollout canary (1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automatic fallback config

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

--
Diego Fernandez
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_onboard_checklist.pdf (1 page)
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@luminahealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: LuminaHealth Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: throughput & cost tuning plan (batching/prefetch/quant/routing)

Diego —

Thanks, this looks good and aligned to what we discussed. We're happy to be pragmatic here: start with a small set of user-facing flows and a background batch route for analytics. A couple quick clarifications:
- Quality threshold: for the clinical summarization route we need > 95% accuracy on entity extraction tests — if 4-bit quant drops us below that we'll fallback to 8-bit.
- Traffic pattern: production average TPS ~3, peak ~18. User sessions are relatively short (4–6 turns).
- Data residency: all inference calls must stay in our org's VPC in us-west-2.

I've attached a small sample of perf traces and the top-12 prompts (anonymized). Also copying procurement to start any needed paperwork.

Attached: lumina_perf_samples.zip (traces + prompts, ~2.3MB)

We can do kickoff Thurs 6/18 at 10am PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Claire
Claire Johnson
Director of Product, LuminaHealth
claire.johnson@luminahealth.com
Attachment: lumina_perf_samples.zip (2.3 MB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: throughput & cost tuning plan (batching/prefetch/quant/routing)

Team —

Claire just shared traces and prompts. Quick, tactical plan below with owners and deliverables (deliverables due EOD Mon 6/22 unless noted):

- Marissa (quantization + eval): run the prompt set on our recommended 4-bit and 8-bit profiles; return a short matrix showing quality delta per prompt and recommended default profile per route. Also include one-sentence risk notes (e.g., hallucination uptick on long clinical summaries).
- Sean (batching + cache): propose initial batching window and max-batch-size for the user-facing route; recommend KV cache TTLs and prefix keys to pre-warm based on prompt clustering from traces. Include simulated latency/cost numbers.
- Karthik (routing/policy + infra): draft a routing policy that implements latency-first for /api/v1/summary and cost-first for /api/v1/bulk-embed. Also list infra prerequisites (VPC peering + IAM role for redwood-agent in us-west-2).
- Diego (CS): coordinate canary schedule and rollout gates; prepare a short rollback playbook (auto-fallback to smaller model variant and trace capture).

Please reply with any constraints I missed. I'm scheduling the kickoff for Thu 6/18 10:00 AM PT and will include a short agenda: goals, deliverables, success metrics, canary plan.

--
Diego
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@luminahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: throughput & cost tuning plan (batching/prefetch/quant/routing)

Diego / team —

Got it. Short notes and ask:
- I will draft the routing policy and a minimal set of fallback model variants by EOD Mon (6/22).
- Infra ask: we need an IAM role with the following minimal permissions for the redwood-agent: ec2:DescribeInstances, ec2:CreateNetworkInterface, sts:AssumeRole, kms:Decrypt (for keys). If Lumina can open a support ticket with their infra team to provision the role, that will speed the first end-to-end test.
- VPC: peering in us-west-2 is fine; we'll want a test subnet with NAT for pulled model caches.

I'll add a short checklist to the Drive folder and link it in the kickoff invite.

On Thu I'll run through an example flow to show how the latency-first route differs in policy from the cost-first route.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@luminahealth.com>

Diego / team —

Thanks — Thurs 6/18 10am PT works for us. Procurement will start the role/IAM request today and I’ve uploaded the first batch of sanitized user prompts to the Drive link.

One ask from our security lead: can Redwood provide a short note describing where quantized model artifacts are stored and what encryption (KMS) is applied? We can share an internal checklist to make sure this is covered in the kickoff.

See you on Thursday.

Best,
Claire
